name: BenefitsBench
note: Made-up situations, no real people. Expected verdicts written from the official rules (GOV.UK, NHS Healthy Start, Brent Council) checked on 30 Oct 2026.

cases.title: Pensioner living alone, council tenant, State Pension only
cases.story: Born 1952, lives alone in a Brent council flat, State Pension is the only income, small savings, a health condition makes daily life harder. Has never claimed anything.

pension-credit.why: Over State Pension age with income under the Guarantee Credit line.

warm-home-discount.why: No qualifying benefit on 23 Aug 2026 yet; opens if Pension Credit is backdated.

attendance-allowance.why: Needs help with daily life; the 6-month need is not asked yet.

cases.title: Pensioner over 75 who already gets Pension Credit
cases.story: Born 1948, lives alone, council tenant, already gets Pension Credit. No health needs mentioned.

council-tax-reduction.why: Guarantee Credit passports to full pension-age Council Tax Reduction.

housing-benefit.why: Guarantee Credit means maximum eligible rent, savings ignored.

free-tv-licence.why: 75 or over and gets Pension Credit.

cases.title: Pensioner who gets Housing Benefit and Council Tax Reduction but not Pension Credit
cases.story: Born 1955, lives alone, council tenant, gets Housing Benefit and Council Tax Reduction, income under the line.

pension-credit.why: Classic missed case: on Housing Benefit, income under the line, never claimed Pension Credit.

warm-home-discount.why: Housing Benefit on the qualifying date counts in England and Wales.

cases.title: Pensioner couple who own their home, good income and savings
cases.story: Both born 1949-1950, own outright, income well over the Pension Credit line, savings over £16,000.

pension-credit.why: No savings limit, but income is well over the line.

council-tax-reduction.why: Pension-age scheme has a £16,000 savings cap.

winter-fuel-payment.why: Paid; HMRC takes it back only if own income is over £35,000.

free-tv-licence.why: 75 or over but no Pension Credit.

cases.title: Mixed-age couple, the person is over State Pension age and the partner is not
cases.story: Born 1956, partner born 1970, renting privately, low income, no benefits yet.

pension-credit.why: One partner under State Pension age: Universal Credit applies instead.

housing-benefit.why: Mixed-age couples cannot make a new Housing Benefit claim; rent help comes through Universal Credit.
housing-benefit.knownRulesGap: precheck leaves Housing Benefit open for a mixed-age couple when the older partner is the one asking.

cases.title: Mixed-age couple, the person is under State Pension age
cases.story: Born 1975, partner born 1958, council tenant, no earnings, small savings.

cases.title: Working parent on low pay with a toddler
cases.story: Born 1990, partner and children including a child under 4, renting privately, take-home earnings £409 to £884 a month, gets Child Benefit.

universal-credit.why: Working does not rule out Universal Credit.

healthy-start.why: Needs Universal Credit with family take-home earnings of £408 a month or less.

cases.title: Universal Credit parent with a child under 4
cases.story: Born 1995, lives with children, child under 4, council tenant, gets Universal Credit and Child Benefit.

warm-home-discount.why: Universal Credit on the qualifying date, bill name not asked yet.

healthy-start.why: On Universal Credit with a child under 4; the £408 earnings line is not asked yet.

cases.title: Pregnant, living alone, not working
cases.story: Born 2000, lives alone, 10+ weeks pregnant, renting privately, no earnings, no benefits yet.

healthy-start.why: Pregnant, but Healthy Start needs Universal Credit (or Pension Credit) first.

cases.title: Full-time carer of someone who gets a disability benefit
cases.story: Born 1980, lives with other adults, council tenant, cares 35+ hours a week, the person cared for gets Attendance Allowance, PIP daily living or DLA care, no earnings.

cases.title: Full-time carer, the person cared for gets no disability benefit
cases.story: As above, but the person looked after does not get Attendance Allowance, PIP daily living or DLA care.

cases.title: Full-time carer who earns over the £204 a week limit
cases.story: Born 1982, lives alone, private rent, cares 35+ hours, cared-for person gets a disability benefit, take-home earnings £885 to £1,083 a month.

carers-allowance.why: Earnings over £204 a week (about £884 a month) after tax and expenses means no Carer's Allowance.

cases.title: Part-time carer, under 35 hours a week
cases.story: Born 1978, lives alone, private rent, cares for a parent but under 35 hours a week, no earnings.

cases.title: Working-age renter with savings over £16,000
cases.story: Born 1985, lives alone, private rent, take-home over £1,083 a month, savings £16,000 or more.

council-tax-reduction.why: Brent working-age scheme caps savings at £6,000.

cases.title: Working-age renter, no earnings, savings between £6,000 and £16,000
cases.story: Born 1988, lives alone, private rent, not working, savings £6,000 to £15,999.

council-tax-reduction.why: Brent working-age scheme caps savings at £6,000.

universal-credit.why: Savings over £6,000 reduce Universal Credit; under £16,000 it can still be paid.

cases.title: Pensioner with low income but savings over £16,000
cases.story: Born 1953, lives alone, council tenant, income under the line, savings £16,000 or more.

pension-credit.why: No upper savings limit; savings over £10,000 count as tariff income (£1 a week per £500).

cases.title: Pensioner who already gets PIP
cases.story: Born 1957, lives alone, owns outright, gets PIP, income around the line.

pension-credit.why: Disability benefits can raise the Pension Credit line.

attendance-allowance.why: Cannot get Attendance Allowance alongside PIP or DLA.

cases.title: Over 75, owns home, needs help with personal care
cases.story: Born 1945, lives alone, owns outright, income around the line, savings £10,000 to £15,999, needs help with daily care.

attendance-allowance.why: No means test; the 6-month need is not asked yet.

free-tv-licence.why: Over 75; free only with Pension Credit.

cases.title: Pensioner in Scotland, renting, needs help with care
cases.story: Born 1950, lives alone in Edinburgh, private rent, income under the line, small savings, health condition.

attendance-allowance.why: Scotland has Pension Age Disability Payment instead.

winter-fuel-payment.why: Scotland has the Pension Age Winter Heating Payment instead.

cases.title: Universal Credit parent in Scotland with a child under 4
cases.story: Born 1992, lives with children, child under 4, council tenant in Glasgow, gets Universal Credit.

warm-home-discount.why: In Scotland it may need an application.

healthy-start.why: Scotland has Best Start Foods instead.

cases.title: Pensioner in Northern Ireland over 75
cases.story: Born 1949, lives alone in Belfast, owns outright, income under the line, health condition.

pension-credit.why: Northern Ireland runs its own Pension Credit.

cases.title: Universal Credit renter in Wales
cases.story: Born 1987, lives alone in Cardiff, private rent, gets Universal Credit.

housing-benefit.why: Universal Credit includes help with rent.

cases.title: Born June 1960, right on the Winter Fuel cut-off
cases.story: Born June 1960 (reached State Pension age in 2026), lives alone, owns outright, income under the line.

winter-fuel-payment.why: Cut-off is 27 June 1960: depends on the day, which Beacon never asks.

cases.title: Born August 1960, not yet at State Pension age
cases.story: Born August 1960, lives alone, has a mortgage, not working, small savings.

pension-credit.why: State Pension age arrives in winter 2026-27.

cases.title: Born May 1960, reached State Pension age in summer 2026
cases.story: Born May 1960, lives alone, council tenant, income under the line.

cases.title: Born February 1961, State Pension age not until 2028
cases.story: Born February 1961, lives alone, private rent, not working, small savings.

cases.title: Care home resident who gets Pension Credit and Attendance Allowance
cases.story: Born 1940, lives in a care home, gets Pension Credit and Attendance Allowance.

council-tax-reduction.why: Council tax is not usually paid in a care home.

winter-fuel-payment.why: Not paid in a council-funded care home while on Pension Credit; funding is not asked.

cases.title: Would rather not give a birth year and is not sure about State Pension age
cases.story: Withheld birth year, not sure about State Pension age, lives alone, private rent, would rather not say savings.

pension-credit.why: Age not settled, so every age-based answer stays Worth checking.

cases.title: Pensioner couple who would rather not share income or savings
cases.story: Born 1954, partner born 1952, council tenant, would rather not say income or savings.

cases.title: Self-employed gig worker with income that goes up and down
cases.story: Born 1993, lives alone, private rent, self-employed, take-home £409 to £884 a month, small savings.

universal-credit.why: Self-employed people can claim; irregular income is assessed monthly.
